If you enjoy easy dinners made with "hamburger" meat, you'll also love Hamburger Steaks with Mushroom Gravy, Hamburger Hashbrown Casserole, and Hamburger Soup!

Sometimes, when I pull a pound of ground beef out of the freezer, I don't want to do anything too involved in order to turn it into dinner. And that's where the nostalgic American classic of Hamburger Gravy saves the day!

This recipe is as easy as browning some ground beef (AKA, hamburger meat) and then whipping up a quick homemade gravy to envelop it, right in the same pan. But the real magic happens when you spoon it onto your plate...over mashed potatoes for the ultimate cozy dinner, or switch things up with noodles, rice, biscuits, and more!

Comfort food doesn't get any simpler than this.

Hamburger Gravy: What to Know

✦ Quick, easy, one-pot. This hearty dinner comes together FAST and with minimal cleanup, making it perfect for busy weeknights.
✦ From-scratch. The creamy, savory gravy is homemade...no canned soup or store-bought gravy packets.
✦ Budget-friendly. Just a few simple, everyday ingredients turn a pound of ground beef into a satisfying dinner.
✦ Old-fashioned comfort food. Nostalgic flavor tastes like something Mom used to make.
✦ Serve it your way. Make your Hamburger Gravy a meal by spooning it over baked or mashed potatoes, egg noodles, rice, toast, biscuits, and more.

Ingredients

You probably already have all the ingredients you need to make Hamburger Gravy in your fridge and pantry!

  • Lean ground beef. You could substitute ground turkey or even ground sausage.
  • Garlic powder + onion powder. This recipe was developed using garlic powder and onion powder so that it can be made as quickly as possible using basic pantry staples. However, feel free to substitute a few cloves of minced garlic and/or ½ cup diced onion instead, cooking it along with the ground beef until softened.
  • Beef base. Or bouillon. To further deepen the savory beef flavor of the Hamburger Gravy. I try to use a brand without artificial ingredients.
  • Worcestershire sauce. For additional umami.
  • All-purpose flour. To thicken the gravy. You could use a gluten-free flour if you prefer.
  • Milk. I make my Hamburger Gravy using whole milk. However, you could use low-fat milk or even a dairy-free milk (like unsweetened almond milk) if you like.
  • Salt + freshly ground black pepper. To taste.

How to Make Hamburger Gravy

(The below photos are intended to be helpful, but please refer to the recipe card at the bottom of this post for FULL DIRECTIONS.)

This effortless dinner can be on the table in 20 minutes flat!

  1. Brown your ground beef and drain the grease.
  1. Add the garlic powder, onion powder, beef base, and Worcestershire sauce. Sprinkle the flour over the beef and cook over low heat, while stirring, until the flour is absorbed.
  1. Slowly stir the milk into the pot and bring to a boil.
  1. Reduce to a simmer and cook until thickened, stirring occasionally.

Serve immediately over your favorite option, from mashed potatoes to biscuits!

Modifications

While milk makes for a traditionally creamy Hamburger Gravy, you can opt to use beef broth instead of half OR all of the milk.

This Hamburger Gravy recipe is intended to be very simple. However, feel free to tweak the basic recipe to your liking. A few ideas for what you might stir in:

✔️ a bit of dried or fresh herbs (such as parsley or thyme).
✔️ a squeeze of mustard or Dijon.
✔️ a dash of red pepper flakes or Sriracha for heat.

Storage + Reheating

Leftover Hamburger Gravy will keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

I don't recommend freezing this recipe since it's milk-based and can separate or turn grainy when thawing and reheating.

To reheat, transfer back to a saucepan and whisk over medium-low heat until simmering and warmed through.

Alternatively, individual portions may be reheated in the microwave. Cover to prevent splattering and reheat in 30-second increments, stirring in between, until heated through.

Sometimes the simplest dinners are the best, and this homemade Hamburger Gravy is proof of that!

It's quick enough for a busy weeknight and made from scratch with simple ingredients, delivering old-fashioned nostalgia without relying on canned soup or a gravy packet.

So serve it the next time you're craving comfort food...and watch it disappear! 🙂

Hamburger Gravy (Quick, Simple, Homemade Meal)

Hamburger Gravy is a simple, comforting, old-fashioned meal that's super quick and easy to make in one pan featuring browned ground beef in a creamy homemade gravy served over mashed or baked potatoes, egg noodles, rice, toast, biscuits, and more!
By Samantha Skaggs
Course: Main Course
Cuisine: American
Prep Time: 5 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 15 minutes minutes
Total Time: 20 minutes minutes
Servings: 4 servings
Calories: 235kcal
Print Pin Rate

Ingredients

  • 1 pound lean ground beef
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1 tablespoon beef base, such as Organic Beef Better Than Bouillon
  • 2 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce
  • 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour
  • 2 cups milk
  • Salt + freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions

  • Set a large skillet, sauté pan, or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook until no longer pink, breaking apart and stirring as the meat cooks. Reduce heat to low and drain the grease.
  • Stir in the garlic powder, onion powder, beef base, and Worcestershire sauce. Sprinkle the flour over the beef and cook for 1 minute, stirring continuously until all of the flour is absorbed.
  • Slowly stir the milk into the pot, bring to a boil, and then reduce to a simmer. Cook for several minutes, stirring occasionally, or until thickened.
  • Stir in a generous amount of black pepper and adjust seasonings to taste, adding salt (or additional beef base) if necessary. Serve Hamburger Gravy hot over mashed or baked potatoes, egg noodles or other pasta, rice, toast or biscuits, or whatever you like.

Equipment Needed

  • Large (3 to 4-quart) Saute Pan

Notes

  • Ground turkey or ground sausage may be substituted for ground beef. However, if using sausage, you may want to reduce the beef base (since both are salty).
  • This recipe was developed using garlic powder and onion powder so that it can be made as quickly as possible using basic pantry staples. However, feel free to substitute a few cloves of minced garlic and/or ½ cup diced onion instead, cooking it along with the ground beef until softened.
  • This recipe was developed using whole milk, but you may use low-fat milk or dairy-free milk (such as unsweetened almond milk) if you wish.
  • While milk makes for a creamy Hamburger Gravy, if you prefer, you may use beef broth in place of half or all of the milk.
  • This recipe is intended to be very simple. However, feel free to tweak the basic recipe to your liking, such as stirring in a bit of dried or fresh herbs (such as parsley or thyme), a squeeze of mustard or Dijon, or a dash of red pepper flakes or Sriracha for heat.
  • Leftovers may be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Freezing is not recommended as milk-based gravies can separate and turn grainy upon thawing/reheating.
  • To reheat, transfer to a saucepan and whisk over medium-low heat until lightly simmering.
  • Or individual portions can be reheated in the microwave. Cover (to prevent splattering) and reheat in 30-second increments, stirring in between, until heated through.
